_comment: Ratchet gates: CI fails only when the count of a known-bad pattern rises
above the committed baseline below. Policy and number change in one diff.
Run: node scripts/ratchet.mjs          (gate — used by CI, non-strict)
node scripts/ratchet.mjs --strict  (also fail on 'slack' — `make ratchet`)
node scripts/ratchet.mjs --list    (print every site, incl. allowed)
node scripts/ratchet.mjs --update  (lower baselines to match reality;
refuses to raise them)
A count BELOW baseline is 'slack': a warning by default (two PRs that each
independently fix one site can both merge cleanly and leave the baseline
stale without turning CI red), and a failure with --strict, which
`make ratchet`/`make quality` use once a baseline is meant to be kept exact.
CI's lint job AND `make pr-check` (`prCheck.ratchets` in agent-lanes.json)
both run non-strict, deliberately: pr-check runs on every unrelated PR, and
strict there would turn every PR red the moment one baseline goes stale from
someone else's already-merged fix, before anyone has run --update. Run
--update to resync the baseline whenever the count legitimately changes.
A count ABOVE baseline ('regression') always fails, strict or not.
Exempt a specific line with an inline comment naming the check it exempts:
`ratchet-allow(<check-id>): <reason>`, written using that file type's
comment syntax (# for .py/.sh, // for js/ts). A pattern check only honors
its own check-id on one of the matched lines; the unreferenced check only
honors its own check-id in the exempted file's first 3 lines. Naming a
different check-id does not exempt. This is a substring/line heuristic,
not real comment parsing — a string literal that happens to contain
`// ratchet-allow(...):`  could still fool it — accepted as a tradeoff,
since any exemption is visible and reviewable in the diff that adds it.
Allowed sites are excluded from the count but still listed separately
with --list.
roots: git-tracked file roots ratchet.mjs scans (via `git ls-files -z -- <roots>`,
NUL-separated so non-ASCII/space-containing paths survive intact).
An empty template (no files under any root) scans 0 files: baseline 0 passes,
baseline > 0 fails as 'scan roots vanished — refusing to pass' (always fatal,
not covered by --strict — a vanished root is a different, worse signal than
ordinary slack).
kind: pattern — whole-file-content regex per extension group. CAUTION: a
quantified group containing overlapping alternatives (e.g. a repeated
`(?:\s|//[^\r\n]*|...)*` where the comment alternative can be split into
multiple equally-valid partitions of the same input) is a classic ReDoS
shape — a run of `//` characters can then take exponential time to fail
to match. Any comment-matching alternative inside a `*`/`+` group must be
unambiguous: a line-comment alternative must consume through its own
line terminator (or end of input) as part of the SAME alternative, e.g.
arbitrary point a sibling alternative could also start from. When
changing a pattern, sanity-check it against a long run of the character
that starts its comment/quantified alternatives before committing.
kind: unreferenced — a testGlobs match is 'orphaned' unless a declared
`runners` entry's `covers` glob matches it AND that runner's `by` string
appears verbatim in one of `wiringFiles` (explicit list only — never
arbitrary files under the scanned roots, so a runner can't be satisfied
by coincidence; full-line `#`-comments in wiring files are stripped
before matching, so a `by` string mentioned only in a comment doesn't
count). A runner whose `by` appears in no (non-comment) wiring text is
itself reported as a violation ('runner not invoked by any wiring file')
so the declaration can't lie about what actually runs it.
`covers` must be narrow enough to match only what `by` actually
executes — e.g. if `by` is a script that runs one named file, `covers`
should name that file, not a `test_*.py` glob over its whole directory,
or a sibling file the script never touches would count as covered and
never actually run.
`by` must be a specific invocation, not a bare word: at least ~6
characters, and containing a `/` or a space (a path, or a command with
an argument). This is enforced in validateConfig so a vague `by` like
"test" is rejected before it can "wire" everything by matching too
broadly.
`wiringFiles` glob entries support only a single `*` confined to the
final path segment (e.g. `.github/workflows/*.yml`) — `**` and `{...}`
brace expansion are rejected by validateConfig rather than silently
resolving to zero files.
To wire a new test area, add a runner, e.g. for a project using pytest
directly with no wrapper script:
{ "covers": ["tests/**/test_*.py"], "by": "pytest tests/" }
`by` just needs to be a substring that genuinely appears in one of the
wiringFiles (a Makefile recipe, a CI step, a package.json script) —
it is not executed by ratchet.mjs itself.
When a project adopts a linter, prefer its native rule over the pattern
entry below (ruff S110 for Python, eslint no-empty for JS/TS) — see
'Enforcement' in .claude/rules/error-handling.md.

patterns.label: python: except swallowed with pass/... (same line or next line, CRLF ok)
